name: demo-api
//implicitDependencies: demo-cli is a real dependency, not just a task-graph edge: the API SHIPS the CLI binary inside its dist (assets/secure), so `nx affected` must rebuild and redeploy the API whenever the CLI changes. A build.dependsOn edge alone would not do that.

metadata.description: The app is assembled entirely by its dependsOn entries, so `build` itself has nothing left to run: it is a pure aggregation node (`nx:noop` -- a bare dependsOn with no executor is invalid, createTask throws). It used to shell out to `npx nx run demo-api:build-base` and then `npx nx run demo-api:copy-cli-artifact` under parallel:false; each of those was a separate Nx process with its own task graph, so nothing deduped the ~80-task ^build chain they share. As edges they resolve in ONE graph.  Ordering is NOT this list -- dependsOn does not order its own entries. build-base -> copy-cli-artifact is enforced by copy-cli-artifact's own dependsOn (build-base's asset copy would otherwise clobber assets/secure); the two manifests write dist/apps/demo-api/*.manifest.json, which no other task in this target touches, so they are genuinely order-free.  `outputs` is empty on purpose: every file under dist/apps/demo-api is written -- and cached, and restored -- by one of the four dependencies. Declaring them here would make a second task own the same paths, which is exactly the one-writer-per-output-directory invariant this whole conversion exists to preserve.  There is no `production` configuration any more: it only existed to swap in `build-base:production`, nothing ever invoked `demo-api:build:production`, and TargetDependencyConfig has no `configuration` field. The production path is `ci-deploy`, which calls `demo-api:build-base:production` directly.

copy-cli-artifact.//: Runs AFTER build-base, never as a build.dependsOn: build-base's own asset copy writes into dist/apps/demo-api/assets and would clobber the CLI if this ran first. build-base's deleteOutputPath:false is what keeps esbuild from wiping the folder at all - load-bearing here exactly as it is for the manifests. This is NOT an `assets` entry on build-base because @nx/esbuild's copyAssets applies the workspace .gitignore, whose /dist line silently makes a dist-rooted asset input copy nothing.

build-watch.//: The watch leg of `serve`. A separate target rather than `build-base --watch` because serve must not shell out to a nested `npx nx`: build-base carries dependsOn ^build, so a nested invocation re-derives and re-runs the whole 23-task chain in its own process -- in the container that raced the Nx daemon into 'Failed to reconnect to daemon after multiple attempts' and the watch leg died, leaving the emulators serving a dist that never rebuilt. As a real target it joins serve's single task graph, where the ^build deps are already satisfied via copy-cli-artifact and get deduped. Options mirror build-base; keep them in sync -- only `watch` differs.

watch-emulators.//: Body lives in watch-emulators.sh so `serve` can run it directly instead of via a nested `npx nx` (which deadlocks -- see the script header).

serve.//: Routed through the task graph rather than nested `npx nx` calls. Previously `nx build demo-api --watch`: run-commands forwards unknown args to EVERY command (forwardAllArgs defaults true), so --watch went to both commands, the first never exited, and with parallel:false copy-cli-artifact never ran -- serving never produced dist/apps/demo-api/assets/secure/demo-cli. Now the manifests and the build+CLI-copy chain are dependsOn entries resolved in ONE task graph, build-watch (continuous) is the rebuild leg, and the emulator loop is invoked as a plain script: any nested `npx nx` here inherits NX_INVOCATION_ROOT_PID and deadlocks against the running serve task.

commands.//: ci-deploy calls build-base directly and bypasses `build` entirely, so it runs none of build's commands or dependsOn targets - the CLI copy has to be repeated here or the deployed function ships without it.
